canonical.name: The Morse complex of the circle: the two arcs between maximum and minimum
canonical.support: Not stated verbatim in any one source; it is the direct two-trajectory instance of the definitions of this pair and of the orientation comparison of Sec. 3.3/Remark 2.5.3(a).

canonical.name: Every broken trajectory is a limit of ordinary trajectories (gluing existence)
canonical.locator: Fowdar Sec. 6 (pre-gluing and existence, Theorems 6.1 and 6.8); Audin--Damian Ch. 3 Proposition 3.2.6; Ritter Lecture 18 Sec. 5.5
canonical.support: The existence half of the gluing construction: ordinary trajectories exist in every prescribed neighbourhood of a broken trajectory, so the compactification is a compactification in the strict sense. The scaffold exposed this as a clause of the compactness theorem; Step 3b split it into a local supplier lemma because the general gluing statement is the analytic input and its scope covers all index drops, not only drop two.

sources.title: Michele Audin and Mihai Damian, Morse Theory and Floer Homology (complete author PDF of the English book, 628 pp.)
sources.locator: Part I Ch. 3 Sec. 3.1-3.4, printed pp. 55-78 (PDF pp. 65-88)
sources.reading_verification: Downloaded the complete 628-page author PDF (2,773,280 bytes) and extracted the full text with mutool. Read Ch. 3 Sec. 3.1-3.4 in full at printed pp. 55-78 (PDF pp. 65-88; the printed page number equals the PDF page number minus ten and was aligned against the running heads): Sec. 3.1 the mod-two chain group and the differential n_X(a,b)=#L(a,b) mod 2, Sec. 3.1.b the partial-sum basis for d^2=0, Sec. 3.1.c the sphere, other-sphere, torus, complex-projective and real-projective examples, Sec. 3.2.a the space Lbar(a,b) of broken trajectories with its neighbourhood basis W(lambda,U-,U+) and the remark that the topology agrees with the quotient topology on L(a,b), Sec. 3.2.b Theorem 3.2.2 (compactness), Lemma 3.2.5 and Corollary 3.2.4 (finiteness for index drop one), Sec. 3.2.c Theorem 3.2.7 (drop two gives a compact 1-manifold with boundary) with Propositions 3.2.8, 3.2.10, 3.2.11 and Lemma 3.2.12 (the collar/branch proof carried out in the standard Morse model), Sec. 3.2.d the boundary/corner remarks, Sec. 3.3 the orientations of the stable manifolds, the induced co-orientations of the unstable manifolds, the oriented moduli spaces and the integer coefficients N_X(a,b), and Sec. 3.4 the independence theorem with the sentence explicitly leaving the boundary-orientation verification to the reader. Formulas, figures 3.1-3.11 and the example counts were checked against the displayed equations.

sources.reading_verification: Downloaded the complete 115-page combined notes (3,097,365 bytes) and extracted text with mutool; located Part III ("Morse Homology") and read Lectures 17-19 at PDF pp. 76-91: Sec. 5.1 the tilted-torus picture (four open subdiagonals, eight broken trajectories, two per interval end, with ends such as alpha_1#alpha_2 and beta_1#beta_3), Sec. 5.2-5.3 the quotient topology on M(p,q), the C^0_loc compactness lemma via Arzela-Ascoli, and the theorem that C^0_loc convergence implies W-convergence using the energy identity f(p)-f(q)=E(u), the no-escape estimate for small remaining energy, and exponential decay at the ends (Hwk 17), Sec. 5.4 the reparametrization trick, the convergence-to-broken-trajectories theorem, the compactness theorem with boundary partial M(p,q)=union M(p,p_2)x...xM(p_N,q), the two stated problems (not every broken flowline need arise, and smoothness), and Sec. 5.5 the gluing theorem (pre-gluing, Picard/implicit function argument, the isotropic embedding, and the statement that sequences converging to a broken trajectory are eventually glued) with the corollary that a one-dimensional moduli space compactifies to a compact smooth 1-manifold with boundary; Lecture 19 Sec. 6.1 defines the mod-two complex, partial p=sum dim M(p,q)=0 #M(p,q) q, finiteness from compactness, and computes partial^2=0. The notes state in Lecture 19 that orientation signs are deliberately omitted from the course, so no oriented result is harvested from this source.

sources.title: Udhav Fowdar, A Functional Analytic Approach to Morse Homology (UCL 4th-year project, 2016; complete PDF)
sources.reading_verification: Downloaded the complete 93-page project PDF (597,056 bytes) and extracted text with mutool; read Sec. 5 "Compactness" at printed pp. 35-44 (Definition 5.1 of compactness up to broken trajectories of order k, the energy bound integral |u'|^2 <= f(x)-f(y), the Arzela-Ascoli step and the compactness theorem), Sec. 6 "Gluing" at printed pp. 44-55 (pre-gluing, Theorems 6.1-6.2 on the surjectivity/gluing isomorphism of the linearized operators, and Theorems 6.8-6.9 that the unparametrised gluing map is a smooth embedding and that sequences converging to a broken trajectory are eventually in its image; also the observation that a component of a relative-index-two moduli space is a circle or an open interval, with exactly two broken ends in the interval case), Sec. 7 "Orientation of space of trajectories" at printed pp. 55-68 (determinant lines of Fredholm operators, Theorem 7.5 on orientation compatibility with gluing, and Theorems 7.6-7.7 on coherent orientations), and Sec. 8 "Morse Homology" at printed pp. 69-75 (characteristic signs tau(u), Definition 8.2 of the integral Morse complex, and the proof of B^2=0 from the opposite products tau(u_1)tau(v_1) = -tau(u_2)tau(v_2) at the two ends of each compactified component).
